similarities.point: Both identify Atella as an ancient Italian town located between Capua and Nola.
similarities.quote_britannica: ATELLA, an ancient town of Gargania in Italy, between Capua and Nespolis.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Atella was an ancient Oscan city of Campania, located 20km directly north of Naples.

similarities.point: Both state that the ruins of Atella are still visible.
similarities.quote_britannica: The ruins of this town are full to be seen about 11 miles from the modern Averfa,
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The ruins of the city walls, private houses, the so-called garden of Virgil and many tombs remain,

similarities.point: Both connect Atella to the Atellan farce.
similarities.quote_britannica: From this town the Atlana fabule, or Atelani Inda, took their name.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The Atellan farce was one of the forms of entertainment of local origin that influenced the Latin theatre.

similarities.point: Both mention that the modern town of Aversa was built from the materials of ancient Atella.
similarities.quote_britannica: which was built out of its materials.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The diocese of Atella continued to exist until it became one of those incorporated into the new see of Aversa, which was founded in 1053.

differences.point: Britannica describes Atella as being in Gargania, while Wikipedia identifies it as an Oscan city of Campania.
differences.quote_britannica: ATELLA, an ancient town of Gargania in Italy, between Capua and Nespolis.
differences.quote_wikipedia: Atella was an ancient Oscan city of Campania, located 20km directly north of Naples.

differences.point: Britannica claims the town's inhabitants were not deemed infamous and retained tribal rights, whereas Wikipedia does not mention this social status.
differences.quote_britannica: The authors thank these forces were not reckoned among the common players, nor deemed infamous , but retained the rights of their tribe,
differences.quote_wikipedia: The Atellan farce was one of the forms of entertainment of local origin that influenced the Latin theatre.

differences.point: Britannica places the ruins 11 miles from Aversa, while Wikipedia details the ruins across several comuni.
differences.quote_britannica: The ruins of this town are full to be seen about 11 miles from the modern Averfa,
differences.quote_wikipedia: The ruins of the city walls, private houses, the so-called garden of Virgil and many tombs remain, on sites in the comuni of Frattaminore, Orta di Atella, Sant'Arpino and Succivo,

wiki_only_topics.topic: Detailed history of Atella during the Roman period and the Second Punic War.
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: Atella was a city of Oscan origin, one of the oldest in Campania and one of the first to have obtained the Roman civitas.
